mechanism: Imagine Trays → Sort Facts → Balance Verdict
title: THE TWO-TRAY TEST

mechanism: Imagine A Pie → Check The Whole → Choose Repair
title: THE BLAME PIE
goal: Owning your part is different from taking all the blame.
steps: 1. Imagine A Pie — Imagine a pie that stands for everything that caused the situation.
2. Share The Slices — In your mind, give slices to your choices, other people, circumstances, systems, timing, and chance.
3. Check The Whole — Make sure all slices together equal 100.
4. Find Your Slice — Focus only on your true share.
5. Choose Repair — Picture one repair for your slice. Let the rest stay outside your responsibility.
win: ✓ My slice stayed mine; the rest went back to the whole pie.
tips: Give self-compassion enough time to change the next moment.
Choose growth first, then decide what self-blame needs.
Choose self-compassion before deciding what self-blame means.
Give self-compassion more authority than self-punishment.
Guilt does not cancel your access to self-respect.

mechanism: Identify Motor → Enter Posture → Decide Consciously

goal: Install a movement the habit cannot do beside.
steps: 1. Identify Motor — Spot the first motor cue—reaching, picking, scrolling, biting, clenching.

win: ✓ Habit vetoed. The choice came back online.

mechanism: Level → Imagine Urge → Choose Time
title: RIDE THE CRAVING GRAPH
goal: An urge is a curve pretending to be a command.
steps: 1. Level — Notice its current level and where it moves in the body.

4. Name Change — When the line changes direction, name the change.
5. Choose Time — Choose what protects the next hour.

win_reward: ✓ The craving curved; the next hour kept the vote.
fullRitual:
RIDE THE CRAVING GRAPH

GOAL
An urge is a curve pretending to be a command.

1. Level — Notice its current level and where it moves in the body.
2. Watch Slope — Watch for slope: rising, flattening, cresting, falling.
3. Imagine Urge — Every thirty seconds, imagine the next point without acting on the urge.
4. Name Change — When the line changes direction, name the change.
5. Choose Time — Choose what protects the next hour.

WIN
✓ The craving curved; the next hour kept the vote.

TIPS
• Give the pull to act less power over decisions that can wait.
• Give a short delay a turn before repeating peak-action deciding.
• Do not turn a craving into a reason for craving escalation.
• Strong urges deserve a delay before they deserve a decision.
• Choose a deliberate response before craving escalation becomes automatic.

MIND BEND
Certainty is a feeling your mind can produce. An urge is a curve pretending to be a command

FORMULA FLOW
Level → Watch Slope → Imagine Urge → Name Change → Choose Time

SAFETY
PAUSE
Cravings linked to withdrawal, overdose, or medical danger require professional help.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

mechanism: Make Two Lanes → Catch The Fight → Drop One Fight
title: PAIN PLUS THE FIGHT
goal: Separate the wound from the fist wrapped around it.
steps: 1. Make Two Lanes — Imagine two lanes: WHAT HURTS and WHAT RESISTANCE ADDS.
2. Keep The Hurt — In the first lane, picture the raw sensation or fact.
3. Catch The Fight — In the second lane, name demands, self-attack, bracing, and impossible arguments with reality.
4. Drop One Fight — Release one item from the resistance lane while respecting the hurt.
win: ✓ Hurt stayed respected while one layer of fighting came off.
tips: Even with shame, you can still choose fair responsibility.
Keep perspective steady while guilt moves through.
Keep self-respect in the room when guilt hurts.
Let perspective guide you when self-punishment starts sounding convincing.
Do not use shame motivation as proof that the inner attack is correct.

mechanism: Open Voices → Name Facts → Use Wisdom
title: THE THIRD VOICE
goal: Emotion and logic are witnesses; wisdom gives the final answer.
steps: 1. Open Voices — Complete three lines.
2. Name Feeling — FEELING SAYS: include its full truth.
3. Name Facts — FACTS SAY: include only verified information.
4. Build Wisdom — WISE RESPONSE: honour the need in the first line and the constraints in the second.
5. Use Wisdom — Read only the third line before acting.

tips: Feelings bring information, not automatic authority over the verdict.

mechanism: Locate Emotion → Track Sensation → Follow Appears
title: EMOTION, COMPLETE YOUR ARC
goal: Feelings move differently when they are not put on trial.
steps: 1. Locate Emotion — Locate the emotion in the body and give it a precise name.
2. Permit — Permit its current intensity without feeding the story.
3. Track Sensation — Track where sensation travels, peaks, breaks, or cools.
4. Follow Appears — Follow until one natural shift appears, then choose the action the situation—not the wave—requires.
win: ✓ The wave moved through; the situation was still there to choose from.
tips: You can respect body tension without obeying body checking.
Let a gentler interpretation interrupt the old pull toward catastrophe scanning.
Checking your body repeatedly can amplify the signal you fear.
Keep a strong sensation separate from your worth.
Let steadiness guide you when body checking starts sounding convincing.

mechanism: Release Forehead → Hold Neutral → Ask Whether
title: THE 2% SOFTENING
goal: Your face can send the body a quieter memo.
steps: 1. Release Forehead — Without forcing happiness, release the forehead, loosen the eyes, and lift the mouth corners by two percent.
2. Keep Expression — Keep the expression believable.
3. Hold Neutral — Hold it while resting your gaze on one neutral visual point.
4. Ask Whether — Ask whether defence changed by even half a notch.

mechanism: Set Code → Reverse Code → Claim Control
title: PLAY THE BODY PASSWORD
goal: A short body code can prove that alarm has not taken every control.
steps: 1. Set Code — Choose three tiny comfortable movements, such as tap a knee, touch a thumb, and shift your gaze.
2. Run Order — Do A–B–C slowly, pausing after each movement long enough to feel it finish.
3. Reverse Code — Do C–B–A at the same pace. If you lose the order, restart instead of speeding up.
4. Claim Control — Name the movement you directed most clearly, then let the code stop.
win: ✓ The body surge lost some of its authority.
tips: Let present-moment facts reduce the pressure that panic creates.
Give a surge of fear its real size, not its emotional size.
Choose safety cues over the short relief of panic fighting.
Choose what supports more control, not what feeds escape rushing.
You can honour a racing sensation and still refuse escape rushing.
mindBend: A loud mental rule is still a mental rule; a short body code can prove that alarm has not taken every control.
formulaFlow: Set Code → Run Order → Reverse Code → Claim Control
safety:
PAUSE

mechanism: Stop Nonessential → Observe Facts → Skip Negotiation
title: THE FOUR-LETTER BRAKE
goal: Crisis speed must pass four gates before action.
steps: 1. Stop Nonessential — S — stop every nonessential movement.
2. Take Physical — T — take one physical step back.
3. Observe Facts — O — observe facts, sensations, and the strongest impulse.
4. Proceed Safely — P — proceed with the smallest safe move that will still make sense in an hour.
5. Skip Negotiation — Do not negotiate with momentum between letters.
win: ✓ Four letters bought enough time to interrupt momentum.
tips: Use a deliberate response to keep the pull to act from becoming everything.
Let self-control grow quietly beside a craving.
Let the urge be difficult without making impulse obedience necessary.
Put choice between the urge and what happens next.
Let more options remain possible even if the urge stays.
mindBend: The first story arrived first, not necessarily best. Crisis speed must pass four gates before action

mechanism: Use Cool → Remove Name → End the Cool
title: COOL THE ALARM PANEL
goal: Temperature can reach body alarm before language does.
steps: 1. Use Cool — Use cool—not painfully cold—water or a wrapped cool pack on the cheeks and around the eyes for a brief interval.
2. Slow — Slow your body while the sensation lands.
3. Remove Name — Remove it, name the room, and reassess the next safe action.
4. End the Cool — Treat the cool sensation as a reset cue. Stop before it becomes an endurance test.
win: ✓ The alarm cooled without turning discomfort into a test.
tips: A racing body needs steadiness more than another frightening interpretation.
One pause can protect safety cues from body scanning.
Let slower breathing reduce the pressure that a racing sensation creates.
When panic rises, return to slower breathing.
Do not abandon settling just because panic is loud.

Boundaries can be measured before they are argued.

win_reward: ✓ Starting became smaller than the story around starting.
fullRitual:
THE BREATH HINGE

GOAL
Rest where one phase becomes another.

1. Follow Inhale — Follow a natural inhale to the instant it turns toward exhale.
2. Leave Hinge Free — Do not hold or stretch the hinge.
3. Change — Notice the same effortless change at the bottom of exhalation.
4. Allow Breaths — Visit each threshold lightly, then allow several breaths to pass unwatched.

WIN
✓ Starting became smaller than the story around starting.

TIPS
• Do not use body scanning as proof that panic is correct.
• Use one safe anchor when a racing sensation starts narrowing your options.
• Body alarms deserve context before they deserve conclusions.
• Choose present-moment facts; you can reassess after panic softens.
• Pause escape rushing; give one safe anchor a fair chance.

MIND BEND
The first story arrived first, not necessarily best. Rest where one phase becomes another

FORMULA FLOW
Follow Inhale → Leave Hinge Free → Change → Allow Breaths

SAFETY
PAUSE
Leave the hinge alone if waiting creates retention or air hunger.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

mechanism: Press Equal → Step Down → Reach Zero
title: MATCH THE PRESSURE, THEN ZERO IT

fullRitual:
THE HUMAN DIAL

GOAL
Let the sensation exist without turning it into a prediction.

1. Name Sensation — Describe the raw sensation without diagnosis or forecast.
2. Locate — Notice where it begins and ends in the body.
3. Widen — Add awareness of two neutral body areas or external sensations.
4. No Checking — Stop repeatedly testing whether the sensation is gone.
5. Reassess Later — Return to normal activity if safe and reassess only after a short interval.

WIN
✓ A body sensation stayed a sensation instead of becoming a whole future.

TIPS
• Intensity can rise without becoming an instruction when you are trying to force your body to calm down.
• Do not demand certainty from a moment that cannot provide it during control struggle.
• Your attention is valuable, so spend it deliberately while control struggle is active.
• Notice what the situation proves before adding what it might mean in this control struggle moment.
• If this only partly helps, follow the part that is still loud after you are trying to force your body to calm down.

MIND BEND
A sensation can be uncomfortable without being a verdict. This moment—you are trying to force your body to calm down—still leaves a next move.

FORMULA FLOW
Name → Locate → Widen → No Check → Reassess

SAFETY
PAUSE
If symptoms may reflect a medical emergency, severe withdrawal, immediate danger, self-harm risk, violence risk, or inability to stay safe, seek urgent professional or emergency help rather than continuing self-help exercises.

1. Orient — Name where you are, what time of day it is, and one thing you can directly see.
2. Do Not Debate — Do not argue with or build on frightening interpretations; return to what you can verify.
3. Human Link — Contact a trusted person, clinician, crisis service, or emergency service appropriate to the risk.
4. Stay Near — Remain with safe people and avoid driving, substances, or major decisions until support is present.

✓ The moment moved from private uncertainty toward shared, verifiable support.

• A strong body signal can still leave room for choice when you may be experiencing severe withdrawal or a medical emergency.
• Let one honest fact carry more weight than mental noise during medical-escalation support.
• Compassion is compatible with clear limits and real responsibility while medical-escalation support is active.
• Let the next action serve your values rather than your loudest impulse in this medical-escalation support moment.
• If this only partly helps, follow the part that is still loud after you may be experiencing severe withdrawal or a medical emergency.
